levels.label: Bioelectronics
levels.claim: Bioelectronic devices couple electronics to the body to monitor and modulate physiological signals.

levels.label: Soft, stretchable bioelectronics
levels.claim: Because skin and tissue are soft and deform, bioelectronics must be soft and stretchable to keep a stable interface.

levels.label: Interconnects
levels.claim: Stretchable interconnects carry every signal between rigid components, so they set the strain limit of the whole system.

levels.label: Limits of rigid metal interconnects
levels.claim: Thin metal films crack at a few percent strain, and geometric designs such as serpentines only buy limited stretchability at the cost of area.

levels.label: Intrinsically stretchable conductors
levels.claim: Conductive polymers and metal-filler elastomer composites stretch intrinsically.

levels.label: Conductivity-stretchability trade-off
levels.claim: Composite conductors lose conductivity under large or cyclic strain because the percolation network of rigid fillers breaks down.

levels.label: Liquid metal
levels.claim: Gallium-based liquid metals combine metallic conductivity with fluidity, so they remain conductive under extreme deformation.

levels.label: Limits of bulk liquid metal
levels.claim: The high surface tension and the oxide skin of bulk liquid metal make it hard to pattern at high resolution with standard printing.

levels.label: Liquid metal particles
levels.claim: Dispersing liquid metal into micro- and nanoparticles yields inks that are compatible with common printing methods.

levels.label: Activation and adhesion problem
levels.claim: As-deposited particle films are insulating because of the oxide shells and need a sintering step, and they adhere weakly to substrates.

levels.label: Surface modification of particles
levels.claim: Modifying the particle surface with ligands or polymers controls stability, adhesion and sintering behaviour.

levels.label: Limits of current surface modifications
levels.claim: Reported surface modifications usually improve one property, such as colloidal stability, while the printed film still needs a separate activation step.

levels.label: Remaining gap
levels.claim: A printable liquid-metal particle ink that adheres strongly to diverse substrates and conducts as printed remains an open problem.

levels.label: This work
levels.claim: This work proposes a surface-modified liquid-metal particle ink for stretchable bioelectronic interconnects (concept level only).
